doc_description: Comprehensive Amcor FY2023 results and FY2024 outlook press release covering June 2023 quarter and full-year GAAP vs non‑GAAP performance (net sales $14.7B; GAAP diluted EPS 70.5 cps; adjusted EPS 73.3 cps), $1.2B returned to shareholders (49.0 cps dividend and $431M buybacks), detailed Flexibles and Rigid Packaging segment trends amid soft demand, destocking and Russia exit headwinds, guidance (FY2024 adjusted EPS 67–71 cps; adjusted free cash flow $850–950M), leverage/interest and tax updates, reconciliations, and conference call details.

structure.title: Amcor reports fiscal 2023 results and provides outlook for fiscal 2024
structure.heading: 1 Amcor reports fiscal 2023 results and provides outlook for fiscal 2024
structure.start_phrase:
Amcor CEO Ron Delia said: “Throughout fiscal 2023, our teams did an excellent job proactively recovering 
inflation and reducing costs in a highly challenging environment.”
structure.summary:
- Focus: Amcor’s fiscal 2023 results, June 2023 quarter EPS, and fiscal 2024 outlook, with CEO commentary and a GAAP/non-GAAP financial comparison.
- June 2023 quarter: GAAP diluted EPS 12.3 cents per share (cps); Adjusted EPS 19.3 cps.
- Fiscal 2023 highlights:
  - Net sales $14.694 billion, flat on a comparable constant currency basis.
  - GAAP net income $1.048 billion; GAAP diluted EPS 70.5 cps.
  - Adjusted EPS 73.3 cps; Adjusted EBIT $1.608 billion.
  - Adjusted free cash flow $848 million (in line with guidance).
  - Shareholder returns $1.2 billion: dividend increased to 49.0 cps; $431 million share repurchases (~3% of shares).
- Fiscal 2024 outlook: Adjusted EPS 67–71 cps; Adjusted free cash flow $850–950 million.
- CEO commentary:
  - Successfully recovered inflation and reduced costs in a challenging environment; modest Adjusted EBIT growth in constant currency.
  - Demand weakened and customer destocking persisted in the last two quarters of FY23.
  - Near-term conditions to remain soft, but pricing for inflation and cost/productivity initiatives expected to improve operating leverage.
  - Headwinds from Russian plant sale and higher interest largely first-half FY24; expecting solid earnings growth in 2H FY24 and a return to high single-digit long-term growth.
  - Continued focus on innovation, sustainability, higher-value markets, value-creating M&A, and shareholder returns.
- Key financials (YoY, FY ended June 30):
  - GAAP: Net sales $14.544B to $14.694B; Net income $805M to $1,048M; Diluted EPS 52.9 cps to 70.5 cps.
  - Adjusted (non-GAAP; Reported % / Comparable constant currency %):
    - Net sales: +1% / ~flat.
    - EBITDA: -5% / +1%.
    - EBIT: -5% / +1%.
    - Net income: -11% / -4%.
    - Diluted EPS: -9% / -2%.
    - Free cash flow: $1,066M to $848M.
- Notes: Non-GAAP excludes non-recurring items; constant currency excludes FX impacts. All figures in USD; rounding may cause totals to differ.

structure.title: Cash Returns to Shareholders
structure.heading: 2 Cash Returns to Shareholders
structure.start_phrase:
Amcor generates significant annual cash flow, maintains strong credit metrics, and is committed to an investment 
grade credit rating.
structure.summary:
- Emphasizes Amcor’s strong annual cash flow, solid credit metrics, and commitment to maintaining an investment-grade rating, enabling reinvestment, acquisitions, and cash returns to shareholders.
- Returned approximately $1.2 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2023 via dividends and share repurchases, alongside completing three bolt-on acquisitions.
- Dividend: Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.1225 per share (up from $0.12), bringing the fiscal 2023 annual dividend to $0.49 per share.
- Dividend payment details: paid in USD for NYSE ordinary shares; ASX CDI holders receive an unfranked A$0.1877 per share (based on a 0.6526 AUD:USD rate over the five trading days ended August 14, 2023). Key dates: ex-div Sept 6, 2023; record Sept 7, 2023; payment Sept 27, 2023.
- Share repurchases: about 41 million shares (~3% of outstanding) bought in fiscal 2023 for $431 million; approximately $70 million planned for repurchases in fiscal 2024 under the existing program.
- Segment results (FY2023 vs FY2022): 
  - Flexibles: sales ~$11.15B (flat), EBIT $1.43B (down; margin 12.8% vs 13.6%).
  - Rigid Packaging: sales $3.54B (up), EBIT $265M (down; margin 7.5% vs 8.5%).
  - Corporate/Other EBIT loss improved to $(86)M from $(105)M.
  - Total Amcor: sales $14.69B (up 1%), adjusted EBIT $1.61B; EBIT margin 10.9% (vs 11.7%); ROAFE 15.4% (vs 16.3%).
- Full-year net sales up 1% reported, reflecting a ~3% FX headwind, ~1% comparability headwind, and ~$775M (about 5%) price increases from raw material pass-through; on a comparable constant currency basis, sales were flat with ~3% price/mix benefit offset by ~3% lower volumes.
- GAAP Net Income was $1,048 million, including a $215 million gain from the sale of the Russia business on December 23, 2022.
- Adjusted EBIT of $1,608 million increased 1% on a comparable constant currency basis; margin of 10.9% includes an approximate 90 bps adverse impact from higher sales dollars tied to raw material pass-through and general inflation.

nodes.title: Dividend
nodes.heading: 2.1 Dividend
nodes.start_phrase:
The Amcor Board of Directors today declared a quarterly cash dividend of 12.25 cents per share (compared with 12.0 
cents per share in the same quarter last year).
nodes.summary:
- Focus on cash returns to shareholders, highlighting Amcor’s strong annual cash flow, solid credit metrics, and commitment to maintaining an investment grade rating while funding organic growth, bolt-on acquisitions, dividends, and buybacks.
- FY2023 shareholder returns: approximately $1.2 billion returned via cash dividends and share repurchases; three bolt-on acquisitions completed.
- Dividend update: quarterly dividend declared at 12.25 cents per share (up from 12.0 cents); FY2023 annual dividend totals 49.0 cents per share. Paid in USD for NYSE ordinary shares; ASX CDI holders receive an unfranked 18.77 AUD cents per share (based on a 0.6526 AUD:USD rate). Key dates: ex-dividend Sep 6, 2023; record Sep 7, 2023; payment Sep 27, 2023.
- Share repurchases: ~41 million shares (~3% of outstanding) bought in FY2023 for $431 million; plan to allocate about $70 million to repurchases in FY2024 under the existing program.
- FY2023 financial results:
  - Net sales up 1% reported to $14.7 billion; headwinds included ~3% FX and ~1% comparability items; about $775 million (≈5%) of price increases from raw material pass-throughs.
  - On a comparable constant currency basis, net sales were flat: price/mix +≈3% offset by ≈3% lower volumes.
  - GAAP Net Income: $1.048 billion, including a $215 million gain from the sale of the Russia business (Dec 23, 2022).
  - Adjusted EBIT: $1.608 billion; up ~1% on a comparable constant currency basis; adjusted EBIT margin 10.9%, pressured by ~90 bps due to higher sales dollars from raw material pass-throughs and general inflation.
  - Segment performance:
    - Flexibles: sales $11.154 billion; EBIT $1.429 billion; margin 12.8% (down from 13.6%).
    - Rigid Packaging: sales $3.540 billion; EBIT $265 million; margin 7.5% (down from 8.5%).
    - Corporate/Other expense: ($86 million) vs ($105 million) prior year.
  - Total adjusted EBIT/Sales margin declined from 11.7% to 10.9%; return on average funds employed decreased from 16.3% to 15.4%.

structure.start_phrase: Net sales for the Amcor Group of $3,673 million were 6% lower than last year on a reported basis.
structure.summary:
- Amcor Group June 2023 quarter: Net sales $3,673m, down 6% reported; FX impact immaterial; ~2% unfavorable items affecting comparability; ~$25m price increases (+1%) from raw material pass-through. Comparable constant currency net sales down ~5% on ~7% lower volumes, partly offset by ~2% price/mix benefits. GAAP Net Income $181m. Adjusted EBIT $436m, down ~7% on a comparable constant currency basis.

Asia Pacific flat; China weaker due to COVID-19 lockdowns; strong growth in India, Australia, pan-Asian healthcare and meat. Latin America low single-digit decline on lower volumes, partly offset by price/mix.

- Flexibles June 2023 quarter: Net sales $2,777m, down 6% reported; FX +~1%, items affecting comparability -~3%, price increases +~$25m (+1%) from raw material pass-through. Comparable constant currency net sales down ~5% (volumes -~7%, price/mix +~2%).

structure.title: June 2023 quarter
structure.heading: 6 June 2023 quarter
structure.start_phrase:

approximately 1% related to movements in foreign exchange rates, an unfavorable impact of approximately 3% related

structure.summary:
- Scope: Amcor Group results for the June 2023 quarter and the twelve months ended June 30, 2023, with segment and regional performance, drivers of change, and interest/tax updates.
- Group (June 2023 quarter):
  - Net sales $3,673m, down 6% reported; approximately 5% lower on a comparable constant currency (ccc) basis.
  - Volume down ~7%, partly offset by ~2% price/mix benefit; FX impact immaterial; ~1% sales growth from raw material pass-through.
  - GAAP Net Income $181m. Adjusted EBIT $436m, down ~7% ccc.
- Flexibles (twelve months ended June 30, 2023):
  - Net sales $11,154m, flat reported; FX -4%, items affecting comparability -2%, +$515m (5%) raw material pass-through; +1% ccc (price/mix +4%, volumes -3%).
  - Regional highlights: North America marginally lower (volume declines offset by price/mix; higher volumes in healthcare, pet care, cheese, home/personal care; lower in condiments, meat, ready meals). Europe low single-digit sales growth (price/mix up; volumes down in coffee, home/personal care, yogurt, confectionery; up in pet care, pharma). Asia Pacific flat (China volumes down due to COVID lockdowns; strength in India, Australia, and pan-Asian healthcare/meat). Latin America low single-digit decline (lower volumes, partial price/mix offset).
  - Adjusted EBIT $1,429m, up ~1% ccc; margin 12.8%, including ~100 bps adverse impact from raw material pass-through and inflation.
- Flexibles (June 2023 quarter):
  - Net sales $2,777m, down 6% reported; FX +1%, items affecting comparability -3%, +$25m (1%) raw material pass-through; ~5% lower ccc (volumes -7%, price/mix +2%).
  - Broad-based volume weakness: high single-digit declines in Europe and North America; mid single-digit decline in Latin America; Asia flat.
  - Adjusted EBIT $387m, lower ccc due to lower volumes, order volatility, unfavorable mix, and cost inflation; partially offset by price and cost actions.
- Rigid Packaging (twelve months ended June 30, 2023):
  - Net sales $3,540m, up 4% reported; FX -1%, +$260m (8%) raw material pass-through; ~3% lower ccc (price/mix +1%, volumes -4%).
  - North America: beverage volumes -6% (hot fill flat on new wins; preform/cold fill down); specialty containers overall down (healthcare, dairy, nutrition up; food and home/personal care down).
  - Latin America: volumes down low single digits amid challenging macro conditions.
  - Adjusted EBIT $265m, lower ccc; margin 7.5%, including ~80 bps adverse impact from raw material pass-through and inflation.
- Rigid Packaging (June 2023 quarter):
  - Net sales $897m, down 5% reported; FX -1%; ~4% lower ccc (volumes -6%, price/mix +2%).
  - North America beverage volumes -8% on soft demand and destocking; hot fill -6%, broadly in line with market.
  - Adjusted EBIT $73m, lower ccc on reduced volumes, order volatility, unfavorable mix, and inflation; partially offset by pricing and cost reduction.
- Market drivers across the period:
  - Soft consumer demand and customer destocking, unfavorable mix, and ongoing cost inflation.
  - COVID-related demand weakness in China; continued strength in India, Australia, and healthcare/meat end markets.
  - Price/mix benefits and pass-through of higher raw material costs partially mitigated volume declines.
- Interest and taxes (full year):
  - Net interest expense $259m, up $124m YoY due to higher rates.
  - GAAP tax expense $193m vs $300m prior year.
  - Adjusted tax expense $250m vs $332m; effective tax rate 18.5% (down from 21.2%) driven by income mix and discrete items.

  - AFCF expected at ~$850–$950 million, representing growth vs. FY2023.
  - Approximately $70 million planned for share repurchases under the existing program.
- Note on forecast uncertainty with reference to the company’s cautionary statement.
- Conference call and webcast scheduled for Aug 16/17, 2023 with global dial-in options and replay available on the company’s website.

structure.title: Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures
structure.heading: 17 Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures
structure.start_phrase:
(1) Calculation of diluted EPS for the three months ended June 30, 2023 excludes net income attributable to shares to be repurchased under forward 
contracts of $1 million, and $1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2022.
structure.summary:
- Purpose: Reconciles Amcor’s Non-GAAP measures (EBITDA, EBIT, Net income, Diluted EPS, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow) to GAAP results and explains adjustments, for the three and twelve months ended June 30, 2022 and 2023.
- Periods covered: Quarterly (Q4/FY quarter) and full fiscal year comparisons for FY2022 vs FY2023.

Key reconciliations and results
- Three months ended June 30:
  - Reported: EBITDA 395 (2022) vs 467 (2023); EBIT 250 vs 323; Net income 109 vs 181; Diluted EPS 7.3c vs 12.3c.
  - Adjusted: EBITDA 609 vs 540; EBIT 505 vs 436; Net income 368 vs 282; Diluted EPS 24.4c vs 19.3c.
  - Adjustments include: 2019 Bemis Integration Plan, net losses on disposals, hyperinflation impacts, property and other (gains)/losses, Russia‑Ukraine conflict impacts, pension settlements, other items, amortization of acquired intangibles, and related tax effects.
  - Adjusted growth vs prior year: EBITDA -11%, EBIT -14%, Net income -23%, EPS -21%; after items affecting comparability (+5–7 pts) and currency (up to +1 pt), comparable constant currency growth: EBITDA -6%, EBIT -7%, Net income -16%, EPS -14%.
  - Adjusted Free Cash Flow: 803 (2022) vs 834 (2023), derived from Adjusted EBITDA less: interest paid net (47 vs 79), income taxes paid (93 vs 95), capex and intangibles (154 vs 144), plus proceeds from asset sales (11 vs 18), movement in working capital (493 vs 572), and other (−16 vs 22).

- Twelve months ended June 30:
  - Reported: EBITDA 1,829 (2022) vs 2,080 (2023); EBIT 1,250 vs 1,510; Net income 805 vs 1,048; Diluted EPS 52.9c vs 70.5c.
  - Adjusted: EBITDA 2,117 vs 2,018; EBIT 1,701 vs 1,608; Net income 1,224 vs 1,089; Diluted EPS 80.5c vs 73.3c.
  - Adjustments include: Bemis integration (FY22), disposals (FY22), hyperinflation, property and other losses, Russia‑Ukraine impacts (including FY23 net gain on disposal of the Russian business and restructuring costs; FY22 impairments and related expenses), pension settlements, other items, amortization of acquired intangibles, and tax effects.
  - Adjusted growth vs prior year: EBITDA -5%, EBIT -5%, Net income -11%, EPS -9%; after items affecting comparability (+3–4 pts) and currency (+2–3 pts), comparable constant currency growth: EBITDA +1%, EBIT +1%, Net income -4%, EPS -2%.
  - Adjusted Free Cash Flow: 1,066 (2022) vs 848 (2023), based on Adjusted EBITDA less: interest paid net (119 vs 248), income taxes paid (256 vs 225), capex and intangibles (527 vs 526), plus proceeds from asset sales (18 vs 30), movement in working capital (−154 vs −229), and other (−13 vs 28).

Notable footnotes and definitions
- Diluted EPS excludes net income attributable to shares to be repurchased under forward contracts ($1m in Q4 FY22 and Q4 FY23; $3m FY22 and $7m FY23).
- Property and other (gains)/losses include South Africa–related insurance recoveries and closure impacts.
- Russia‑Ukraine impacts encompass impairments and restructuring in FY22 and net gain on disposal plus restructuring in FY23.
- Amortization relates to acquired intangibles from business combinations.
- Items affecting comparability reflect acquired, disposed, and ceased operations.

structure.title: Reconciliation of adjusted EBIT by reporting segment
structure.heading: 18 Reconciliation of adjusted EBIT by reporting segment
structure.start_phrase:
Property a nd other (gains)/losses, net for the three months ended June 30, 2023 includes property claims and losses, net of insurance recovery 
related to the closure of our business in South Africa.
structure.summary:
The excerpt summarizes Amcor’s reconciliation of adjusted EBIT by reporting segment (Flexibles, Rigid Packaging, and Other) and a net debt reconciliation, covering both the three months and twelve months ended June 30, 2022 and 2023.

Key elements:
- Reconciliation from net income to EBIT and to adjusted EBIT by segment, detailing specific adjustments: 2019 Bemis Integration Plan costs, losses on disposals, hyperinflation impacts, property and other gains/losses (notably tied to South Africa facility closure and prior Durban unrest), Russia-Ukraine conflict impacts (impairments/restructuring in FY22; net gain on sale and offsetting costs in FY23), pension settlements, other items, and amortization of acquired intangibles.
- Three months ended June 30:
  - Adjusted EBIT declined to $436m in 2023 from $505m in 2022 (-14%).
  - Segment detail: Flexibles $387m (-14%); Rigid Packaging $73m (-24%); Other -$24m.
  - Adjusted EBIT margins softened: total 11.9% (from 12.9%), Flexibles 13.9% (from 15.1%), Rigid 8.1% (from 10.1%).
  - Bridge to comparable constant currency growth shows total adjusted EBIT down 7% cc; Flexibles down 7% cc; Rigid down 23% cc, with items affecting comparability and currency quantified.
- Twelve months ended June 30:
  - Adjusted EBIT declined to $1,608m in FY23 from $1,701m in FY22 (-5%).
  - Segment detail: Flexibles $1,429m (-6%); Rigid Packaging $265m (-8%); Other -$86m.
  - Adjusted EBIT margins declined: total 10.9% (from 11.7%), Flexibles 12.8% (from 13.6%), Rigid 7.5% (from 8.5%).
  - Comparable constant currency growth bridge indicates total +1% cc for FY23 (Flexibles +1% cc; Rigid -7% cc), with separate disclosure of currency and items affecting comparability.
- Net debt reconciliation:
  - Net debt increased to $6,057m at June 30, 2023 (cash and cash equivalents $689m; short-term debt $80m; current portion of long-term debt $13m; long-term debt $6,653m) from $5,715m at June 30, 2022.
- Footnotes clarify the nature of adjustments, including South Africa-related insurance recoveries/losses, Russia business sale and related initiatives, and that “items affecting comparability” reflect acquired, disposed, and ceased operations.
